# Calligra legacy matcher adapter experiment

Project-owned callable/CommonJS API glue for the build-only consumers that require the minimatch 3/5 export shape. Every match, pattern parse and brace expansion delegates to the actual fixed minimatch 11.0.1 package, installed under the explicit `minimatch-modern` npm alias. No old minimatch parser is copied, renamed or assigned a fake fixed version. This package has its own private name and version.

The `optimizationLevel: 0` default and disabled row merging preserve the segment arrays consumed by glob 7. Project-owned proxy views supply the legacy `_glob` metadata and `Symbol.match` protocol; every test delegates to the fixed nonrecursive Matcher, and shared cached Matchers are not modified. Explicit caller options take precedence. Security bounds come from the fixed underlying parser. Modern named-export consumers should use minimatch 11 directly instead of this adapter.

The adapter must pass differential matcher and real glob 7 filesystem tests, bounded adversarial input, normal clean installation, the existing zero desktop audit, and actual Windows installer/packaged-renderer validation before adoption. This experiment is not a published npm package or a completed application fix.

The actual installed-consumer regression covers glob 7 recursive traversal and Unicode/dotfiles, filelist root-pattern exclusions, dir-compare content/include filters, ASAR packing and unpacked native paths, and the named-export API used by modern electron-builder/universal. A separate differential experiment covers minimatch 3.1.5 and 5.1.9 against the fixed engine (2,640 boolean cases and 15 filesystem patterns). On Windows the original filelist 1.0.6 already fails its normalized recursive `**/*.txt` pattern; the original and adapted trees both return an empty list. That pre-existing limitation is recorded rather than claimed fixed. Actual installer and renderer gates remain required.

The npm dependency key `minimatch` explicitly aliases this project-owned package; its package.json and lock retain the real `calligra-legacy-matcher` name and independent version. Four legacy consumers use the root reference; named-export consumers use the actual upstream 11.0.1 package directly. The archive contains only this source, manifest, README and the exact canonical project GPL license, with source/archive equality checked before CI installation. It is never published to npm.
